correctness.rationale: A common target forces pairwise source distance strictly below \(\sqrt2\), hence at most two adjacent preimages. The horizontal and vertical collision rectangles follow directly from half-open floor inequalities. The primitive Pythagorean modular matrix has cyclic rank-one image of cardinality q; a ninety-degree phase symmetry pairs every nonzero horizontal residue with a vertical residue, proving \(H=V+1\). Orthogonal primitive Gaussian-integer generators of norm \(\sqrt q\) give a square lattice of covolume q and Voronoi radius sqrt(q/2), establishing the explicit discrepancy bound. Rotation preserves area up to \(O(M)\) lattice-boundary error, forcing equal densities of zeros and double preimages. The standalone script independently checked 110 ordered triples, q-by-q complete phases and finite target multiplicities; enumeration is not used as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The nonresonant first-preimage density is already exactly given by Vladimirov (Theorem 19(d)); it is expressly attributed as prior. Hannusch–Pethő supply the lower positivity result and the rational modular setup, but not the explicit all-Pythagorean density spectrum with odd numerator and a universal \(O(q^{-1/2})\) convergence bound. Inverse-multiplicity and quantizer-aliasing synonym searches were made against public primary sources and mathematical results records. The residual concern is implicit earlier coverage in the extensive older quantization literature, not a known dominating theorem for the rational case.
residual_risks: The finite modular description is close to the rational phase arithmetic developed by Hannusch–Pethő; an equivalent parity/square-lattice estimate could be implicit in still earlier quantizer-frequency work.

value.rationale: Inverse-image hole density is a natural dynamical measure of loss of invertibility explicitly studied in the cited source literature. Pythagorean rotation angles are a dense natural arithmetic resonance class omitted by the generic theorem. The theorem completely determines their exact densities via one finite modular count, proves the odd-numerator restriction, and quantitatively controls the resonance defect by an all-denominator \(O(q^{-1/2})\) law; for 3/4/5 it detects a real gap of \(1/25\) from the generic value. These are substantive geometry/number-theory interactions in a canonical discretized dynamical system, not a renaming or arbitrary parameter restriction.
